subject: Remediation proposal and onboarding credit for FableApps — service impact Aug 18
messages:
From: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@fableapps.co>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Severe latency/dropped calls during onboarding window (Aug 17-18)

Hi Rishi,

We hit a pretty disruptive window last night during our onboarding tests with Redwood. Between ~22:40 and 23:15 PDT on Aug 17 we saw a spike in 500s and timeouts for inference requests; retrying created request storms that made the experience unusable for a portion of our QA team. We rely on predictable latency for our feature flag rollout and this set us back by a whole day of go/no-go testing.

Can you confirm what happened on your side? From our logs there were persistent 10–12s tail latencies and ~18% error rate during the window. We’d like to discuss remediation — token credits and possibly a short trial extension while we finish onboarding. Our procurement team will need a written proposal to approve any goodwill credits.

Thanks — please loop in anyone who needs to see this.

— Alex
Alex Duarte
Head of Platform, FableApps
alex.duarte@fableapps.co

Attachment: fableapps_qalog_20260817.zip (log bundle stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Duarte <alex.duarte@fableapps.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency/dropped calls during onboarding window (Aug 17-18)

Hi Alex — thanks for the report and the log bundle. I’m really sorry this disrupted your onboarding run.

Quick update: I’ve escalated to the infra team and tagged this INF-4312 for postmortem; we’re pulling request traces to identify the root cause (likely a transient autoscaling mismatch + a KV cache invalidation that amplified cold-paths). Marissa — looping you in so we can coordinate the customer-facing remediation/credit.

From a next-steps standpoint:
- We’ll deliver a short incident summary + rollback path by EOD tomorrow (Aug 19).
- I’ll propose a remediation package (token credit + trial extension) for your procurement team to review.
- If it helps, we can also offer a live 30-minute review with infra and your engineers to go over traces.

Would a formal statement and proposed addendum sent to procurement suffice for now?

I’ll follow up once infra confirms the timeline. Apologies again for the friction here.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Mobile: +1 415-555-0192

Proposal (internal recommendation):

Thanks for the draft, Marissa.

Approve with a small uplift: increase the token credit to 60,000 and extend the trial period to 45 days. The uplift is intended to remove negotiation friction and demonstrate we prioritize resilience for early-stage partners. Legal should execute a lightweight addendum (no pricing changes) — loop in legal, get DocuSign, and we can finalize this today.

Please ensure the incident summary clearly states the root cause (autoscale + cache invalidation) and the mitigation steps we’ve implemented (permanent autoscale tuning + a KV cache warm path). We don’t want repeat surprises.

Soojin Lee
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — thanks again for the patience while we investigated. Attached is our formal remediation package and the proposed addendum for procurement:

Summary of offer (final):
- Account credit: 60,000 generation tokens applied to FableApps account, viewable on your billing page at next invoice.
- Trial extension: 45 days added to your onboarding trial window to complete validation runs.
- Technical support: one 60-minute troubleshooting session with our infra team (scheduled at your convenience).

Attachments: incident_report_20260818.pdf (postmortem), proposed_credit_addendum.docx (addendum with DocuSign stub).

Next steps: please review the addendum and confirm procurement contact for DocuSign. Once signed we’ll apply the credit and extend the trial within 24 hours. If you’d like the infra session before signing, indicate preferred times and we’ll set it up.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ve implemented autoscale tuning and a KV cache warm path to stop this class of regression. We’ll follow up with a short validation run and postmortem summary.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
